name: Cured hide
description: A scraped and cured animal hide rolled tight and tied with cord. It still needs tanning before it is leather.
notes: Rolled 200 mm long and 28 mm across; skin-rawhide draws the outer side and beeswax the paler scraped side seen in the spiral ends. Tanning it into leather has no content field yet.

name: Cured pelt
description: A cured animal skin with its fur still on, rolled fur side in and tied with cord. It still needs tanning.
notes: Rolled 170 mm long and 60 mm across, fur-brown showing in the spiral ends and as tufts. Tanning it into fur has no content field yet.

name: Denim patch
description: A hemmed square of blue denim, for mending or for sewing into larger sheets.
notes: 150 mm square with paler running stitches round the hem. The cloth is thinner than the 2 mm voxel grain, so the drawn sheet is thicker than real denim.

name: Felt patch
notes: 150 mm square, 2 mm thick, in felt-grey.

name: Fur patch
description: A square of fur on its leather backing, for mending fur clothing or piecing into sheets.
notes: 150 mm square: a leather-tan back and fur-brown tufts. The faux fur variant shares this model with fur-pale on its fur slot.

name: Faux fur patch
description: A square of synthetic fur on a fabric backing, for mending or piecing into sheets.
notes: Variant of the fur patch; same model with pale fur.

name: Gambeson batting
description: A loose wad of shredded rags, dry grass and hair, used to stuff padded armour.
notes: One lumpy mound about 65 mm across and 30 mm high mixing cloth-rag, straw-pale and fur-brown lumps, with grass stalks poking out. Stuffing a gambeson with it has no content field yet.

name: Grass yarn
description: A ball of coarse yarn twisted from dry grass. Too thick to sew with, but it can be woven.
notes: A ball 80 mm across in straw-rope with jute windings and a loose end. Weaving it into cloth has no content field yet.

name: Kevlar patch
description: A loosely woven square of golden Kevlar, for mending cut-resistant clothing.
notes: 150 mm square in aramid-gold with raised weave threads both ways and fraying edges. The cloth is thinner than the 2 mm voxel grain, so the drawn sheet is thicker than the real cloth.

name: Leather patch
description: An unevenly cut square of brown leather, for mending and small leatherwork.
notes: About 150 mm across with ragged cut edges, 2 mm thick in leather-brown.

name: Nomex patch
description: A hemmed square of flame-resistant cloth.
notes: 150 mm square in knit-fr with cloth-turnout stitching; a flat woven fire-resistant cloth finish would read truer. The cloth is thinner than the 2 mm voxel grain, so the drawn sheet is thicker than the real cloth.

name: Rigid Kevlar plate
description: A stiff panel of Kevlar layers set in resin, for mending hard armour.
notes: 300 by 250 mm and 12 mm thick with rounded corners; resin-honey lines on the edge show the layers. No epoxy-set aramid finish exists, so aramid-gold stands in. Repair use has no content field yet.

name: Kevlar scraps
description: A few small offcuts of Kevlar cloth, worth unpicking for thread.
notes: A heap of five aramid-gold offcuts about 45 mm across. The offcuts are thinner than the 2 mm voxel grain, so the drawn sheet is thicker than the real cloth.

name: Nomex scraps
description: A few small offcuts of flame-resistant cloth, worth unpicking for thread.
notes: Shares the offcut heap shape with the aramid scraps, in knit-fr. The offcuts are thinner than the 2 mm voxel grain, so the drawn sheet is thicker than the real cloth.

name: Canvas sheet
description: A hemmed sheet of waxed canvas, tough enough for bags and outer clothing.
notes: 610 by 305 mm laid flat in cloth-canvas with a canvas-grey hem and one corner turned back. The cloth is thinner than the 2 mm voxel grain, so the drawn sheet is thicker than the real cloth.

name: Patchwork canvas sheet
description: A canvas sheet pieced together from six odd panels.
notes: 610 by 305 mm laid flat; panels alternate cloth-canvas, canvas-grey and cloth-khaki with cord-cotton seams. The cloth is thinner than the 2 mm voxel grain, so the drawn sheet is thicker than the real cloth.
